What is Paid UGC? (And Why It's Different from Influencer Marketing)

Paid UGC is when brands pay you to create content they own and use in their marketing — ads, website, social media, email campaigns. The key differences from traditional influencer work:

  • You don't need followers: Brands want authentic content, not reach. Many UGC creators have under 1,000 followers.
  • You get paid upfront: Typical rates are $50-$150 per short video, $200-$500+ for ad packages.
  • Content is for their channels: You create it, they post it on their ads and pages.
  • No posting required: You don't need to post on your own account (though some deals include both).

This makes UGC perfect for creators who want to earn money without building a massive following.

How to Pitch Brands for Paid UGC

Getting paid UGC work is different from influencer outreach. Here's what works in 2026:

1. Build a UGC Portfolio First

Before pitching, create 3-5 spec (unpaid sample) videos showing your style. These should be:

  • 15-60 seconds long
  • Vertical format (9:16)
  • Good lighting and audio
  • Natural, not overly polished
  • Include hooks and calls-to-action

2. What to Include in Your UGC Pitch

  • Portfolio link: Google Drive or portfolio site with your best UGC samples
  • Content types: Specify what you create (unboxing, testimonials, tutorials, etc.)
  • Turnaround time: Most brands want content within 7-14 days
  • Your rates: Be upfront about pricing (or ask for their budget)
  • Usage rights: Clarify if rates include ad usage vs. organic only

3. Where to Find UGC Jobs

  • Direct pitch: Email brands using the contacts in this list
  • UGC platforms: Billo, Insense, JoinBrands, Trend.io
  • newcollab: Brands browse creator profiles and send UGC requests directly
  • Twitter/X: Search "UGC creator needed" or "looking for UGC"

FAQ

Do I need followers to get paid UGC work?

No. UGC is about content quality, not reach. Many successful UGC creators have under 1,000 followers. Brands care about your video skills, authenticity, and ability to match their target demographic — not your follower count.

How is UGC different from influencer marketing?

Influencer marketing pays you to post on YOUR account to YOUR audience. UGC pays you to create content brands post on THEIR accounts and ads. You don't need an audience for UGC — you just need to create compelling content.

Do brands provide the products for UGC?

Usually yes. Most brands ship products for free before you create content. Some offer a product allowance ($50-$200) to purchase items yourself. Always clarify product sourcing before accepting a project.

What equipment do I need for UGC?

Smartphone (iPhone 12+ or equivalent), ring light or natural window light, and a quiet space. That's it. Brands want authentic, relatable content — not cinematic production. Most successful UGC is shot on phones.

How fast do UGC creators get paid?

Payment terms vary: some brands pay 50% upfront + 50% on delivery, others pay Net 15 or Net 30 after content approval. Always agree on payment terms before starting work. Use contracts for projects over $200.
